agyos_skill.intent: Transform high-level vibe coding prompts and non-technical ideas into production-grade, FAANG-level software with automated PRD synthesis, TDD, threat modeling, and design engineering.
agyos_skill.instructions: The definitive bridge between high-level, natural language "vibe coding" prompts and FAANG-grade, enterprise-ready software systems. When non-technical founders, general operators, or rapid "vibe coders" express an ambitious product idea ("Build me an analytics dashboard with Stripe subscriptions and Google auth"), standard LLMs frequently produce fragile prototypes: monolithic 1,200-line files, hardcoded credentials, missing database indices, race conditions, and zero test coverage. This skill equips AGYOS to act as a virtual FAANG engineering department, autonomously promoting rapid vibe prototypes into robust, hardened, production-grade applications. ``` [Vibe Prompt] ➔ [1. SHAPE SPEC] ➔ [2. CONTRACTS & ADR] ➔ [3. TDD MAKER] ➔ [4. VIBE AUDIT] ➔ [5. VERIFY] ``` Convert loose, conversational intent into a structured Task List with unambiguous acceptance criteria: 1. **Core User Story**: Who is the user and what is the exact outcome? 2. **Acceptance Criteria**: Verifiable statements of done (e.g. "Returns HTTP 200 with JWT token on valid credentials"). 3. **Declared Scope Boundary**: Explicitly document what is **in-scope** vs **out-of-scope** to prevent feature creep. 4. **Complexity Scoring**: Call `bin/agyos decide "<task>"` to obtain the calibrated complexity score (1–5). Before writing application logic: 1. **Schema-First Data Contracts**: Define typed data models (Pydantic in Python, Zod in TypeScript, Serde in Rust) with boundary validation. 2. **Database Invariants**: Ensure every queried foreign key has an index; enforce idempotency keys on write endpoints. 3. **Architecture Decision Record (ADR)**: If introducing a new library or structural change, record the decision in `docs/adr/`. 4. **Blast Radius Containment**: Isolate failures so that external service timeouts do not crash the primary application. Execute autonomous Test-Driven Development (TDD): 1. **Write Failing Test (RED)**: Author an Arrange-Act-Assert (AAA) test capturing the required behavior. 2. **Minimal Implementation (GREEN)**: Write the minimal clean code to make the test pass. 3. **Refactor & Polyglot Discipline (IMPROVE)**: - Functions under 50 lines with single responsibility. - Files under the 800-line maintainability ceiling. - Immutability: return new copies; never mutate arguments or state in-place. - Maximum 4 levels of indentation; early guard returns.
